questions.stem: A Service Catalog may include which of the following components?

options.text: Order Guides, Catalog Items, and Interceptors
Catalog Items, Asset Contracts, Task Surveys
Record Producers, Order Guides, and Catalog Items

questions.explanation: The Service Catalog includes Record Producers (creates task records), Order Guides (bundles multiple items), and Catalog Items as its three main component types (D). Exchange Rates (A), Interceptors (B), and Asset Contracts (C) are not Service Catalog components.

questions.stem: Which one of the following statements applies to a set of fields when they are coalesced during an import?

options.text: If a match is found using the coalesce fields, the existing record is updated with the information being imported
If a match is not found using the coalesce fields, the system does not create a Transform Map
If a match is found using the coalesce fields, the system creates a new record
If a match is not found using the coalesce fields, the existing record is updated with the information being imported

questions.explanation: When a coalesce field match is found, the existing record is updated with the imported information (A). If no match is found, a new record is created. Creating a new record on match (C) and updating on no match (D) are incorrect. Coalesce does not affect Transform Map creation (B).

questions.stem: As it relates to ServiceNow reporting, which of the following statements describes what a metric can do?

options.text: A metric is a report gauge used on homepages to display real-time data
A metric is a time measurement used to report the effectiveness of workflows and SLAs
A metric is used to measure and evaluate the effectiveness of IT service management processes
A metric is a comparative measurement used to report the effectiveness of flows and SLAs.

questions.explanation: A metric is used to measure and evaluate the effectiveness of IT service management processes (C). A homepage gauge (A) describes report gauges specifically. Time measurement for workflows/SLAs (B, D) is too narrow — the platform definition of metric is broader.

questions.stem: The display sequence is controlled in a Service Catalog Item using which of the following?

options.text: The Default Value field in the Catalog Item form
The Sequence field in the Catalog Item form
The Order field in the Variable form
The Choice field in the Variable form

questions.explanation: The display sequence of variables in a Catalog Item is controlled by the Order field on the Variable form (C). The Default Value field (A) sets a default. The Sequence field (B) does not exist. The Choice field (D) defines picklist options, not ordering.

questions.stem: Reports can be created from which different places in the platform? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Reports can be created from a list column heading (A) by right-clicking a column header, and from the View/Run module (D) under the Reports application. The Metrics module (B) and Statistics module (C) are for system metrics/stats, not directly creating reports.

questions.stem: Knowledge Base Search results can be sorted by which of the following? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Knowledge Base search results can be sorted by Most recent update (A), Relevancy (C), and Number of views (E). Popularity (B) is not a listed sort option. Manager assignment (D) is not a sort criterion for knowledge search results.

questions.stem: What is the path an Administrator could take to view the fulfillment stage task list for an order placed by a user?
questions.explanation: The order path is: REQ (order/request) > RITM (Requested Item) > TASK (fulfillment task) (C). The path cannot start with RITM (A). There is no PROCUREMENT or FULFILLMENT prefix number in the standard fulfillment path (B, D).

questions.stem: Which term refers to application menus and modules which you may want to access quickly and often?
questions.explanation: Favorites are application menus and modules you want to access quickly and often (B). Breadcrumbs (A) show navigation path. Tags (C) categorize/flag records. Bookmarks (D) are not a standard ServiceNow navigator feature in this context.

questions.stem: What is generated from the Service Catalog once a user places an order for an item or service?
questions.explanation: When a user orders a catalog item or service, the Service Catalog generates a Request (REQ) record (C). It does not generate a change request (A) by default. An Order Guide (B) is what the user orders, not what is generated. SLAs (D) are not generated by ordering.

questions.stem: From the User menu, which actions can a user select? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: From the User menu (top-right), users can select Log Out (B), Elevate Roles (C), and Impersonate Users (D). Send Notifications (A), Order from Service Catalog (E), and Approve Records (F) are not User menu options.

questions.stem: Buttons, form links, and context menu items are all examples of what type of functionality?
questions.explanation: Buttons, form links, and context menu items are all examples of UI Actions (B). Business Rules (A) run server-side scripts. Client Scripts (C) run browser-side. UI Policies (D) control field behavior. UI Actions add interactive elements to forms and lists.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true of Service Catalog Items in relation to the Service Catalog?
questions.explanation: Catalog Items are the building blocks of the Service Catalog (B). They execute when requested (not behind the scenes — A). They are required for a functioning catalog (not optional — C). They define orderable items, not just options (D).

questions.stem: Table Access Control rules are processed in the following order:

options.text: any table name (wildcard), parent table name, table name
table name, parent table name, any table name (wildcard)
parent table name, table name, any table name (wildcard)
any table name (wildcard), table name, parent table name

questions.explanation: Table Access Control rules are evaluated from most specific to least specific: table name → parent table name → wildcard/any table name (B). Wildcard is the fallback and is evaluated last, not first (A, D). Parent is evaluated between table and wildcard.

questions.stem: What is the platform name for the User table?
questions.explanation: The platform table name for the User table is sys_user (D). u_users (A) would indicate a custom table. sys_users (B) is incorrect — it is not plural. x_users (C) suggests a vendor-scoped table. sys_user is the correct platform name.

questions.stem: A REQ number in the Service Catalog represents`¦

options.text: the individual item in the order.

questions.explanation: REQ represents the order number — the top-level Request record (A). RITM (D) represents individual items within the order. The stage (B) is a field within REQ/RITM. Tasks (C) are at the TASK level, one level below RITM.

questions.stem: Which would NOT appear in the History section of the Application Navigator?
questions.explanation: The History section shows recently visited Records (A), Lists (C), and Forms (D). UI Pages (B) are developer/admin resources and do not appear in History — users navigate to them via modules, not by browsing.

questions.stem: Which one of the following statements is a recommendation from ServiceNow about Update Sets?

options.text: Avoid using the Default Update set as an Update Set for moving customizations from instance to instance
Before moving customizations from instance to instance with Update Sets, ensure that both instances are different versions
Use the Baseline Update Set to store the contents of items after they are changed the first time
Once an Update Set is closed as ג€Completeג€, change it back to ג€In Progressג€ until it is applied to another instance

questions.explanation: ServiceNow recommends avoiding the Default Update Set for moving customizations (A) as it may accumulate unrelated changes. Both instances should be the same version (B is wrong). There is no Baseline Update Set (C). Closed Complete sets should not be reopened (D).

questions.stem: Which of the following is used to initiate a flow?
questions.explanation: A flow is initiated by a Trigger (A), which defines when and under what conditions the flow starts. Core Actions (B) are steps within a flow. Spokes (C) provide integration capabilities. Events (D) can be a type of trigger but are not the initiator itself.

questions.stem: For Administrators creating new Service Catalog items, what is a characteristic they should know about Service Catalog variables?

options.text: Service Catalog variables can only be used in Record Producers
Service Catalog variables can only be used in Order Guides
Service Catalog variables cannot affect the order price
Service Catalog variables are global by default

questions.explanation: Service Catalog variables are global by default (D), meaning they can be shared across multiple catalog items and variable sets. They are not limited to Record Producers (A) or Order Guides (B). Price-affecting variables exist (C is wrong).

questions.stem: Which one of the following statements is true about Column Context Menus?

options.text: It displays actions such as creating quick reports, configuring the list, and exporting data
It displays actions related to filtering options, assigning tags, and search
It displays actions related to viewing and filtering the entire list
It displays actions such as view form, view related task, and add relationship

questions.explanation: The Column Context Menu displays actions such as creating quick reports, configuring the list, and exporting data (A). Filter options are in the filter bar (B). C describes the list view itself. D describes record context menus (view form, relationships).

questions.stem: Which ServiceNow products can be used to discover and populate the CMDB? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: ServiceNow Discovery (A) scans network infrastructure to find and populate CIs. IntegrationHub ETL (B) imports third-party data into the CMDB. Finder (C) is not a ServiceNow product. CMDB Plug-in (D) and CMDB Integration Dashboard (E) do not populate the CMDB.

questions.stem: When using the Load Data and Transform Map process, what is the Mapping Assist used for?

options.text: Mapping fields using the Import Log
Mapping fields using a Field Map

questions.explanation: The Mapping Assist tool maps source fields to target fields using a Field Map (D). It does not use Import Log (A), Transform History (B), or SLAs (C) for field mapping. Field Maps define source-to-target column mappings.

questions.stem: Which one of the following statements describes the contents of the Configuration Management Database (CMDB)?

options.text: The CMDB contains data about tangible and intangible business assets
The CMDB contains the Business Rules that direct the intangible, configurable assets used by a company
The CMDB archives all Service Management PaaS equipment metadata and usage statistics
The CMDB contains ITIL process data pertaining to configuration items

questions.explanation: The CMDB contains data about both tangible assets (hardware like servers, routers) and intangible assets (software, services, contracts) (A). Business Rules (B) are not stored in the CMDB. PaaS equipment metadata (C) is too narrow. ITIL process data (D) is in ITSM tables.

questions.stem: In what order should filter elements be specified?
questions.explanation: Filter conditions must be specified in the order: Field → Operator → Value (A). This mirrors query structure: select a field, choose a comparator, enter the value. Operator before Field (C) and Value before Field (D) are incorrect orderings.

questions.stem: Which statement is true about business rules?

options.text: A business rule must run before a database action occurs
A business rule can be a piece of Javascript
A business rule must not run before a database action occurs
A business rule monitors fields on a form

questions.explanation: A business rule can be a piece of JavaScript (B) — the Script field accepts server-side JavaScript. Business rules can run before, after, async, or display (A is wrong — not just before). They run server-side (D is wrong — client scripts monitor form fields).

questions.stem: Which of the following are a type of client scripts supported in ServiceNow? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: The four supported types are onSubmit (A), onCellEdit (C), onLoad (D), and onChange (F). onUpdate (B), onEdit (E), and onSave (G) are not valid client script types in ServiceNow.

questions.stem: Which type of tables may be extended by other tables, but do not extend another table?
questions.explanation: Base Tables (A) are at the top of the hierarchy — they can be extended by others but do not extend another table. Core Tables (B) extend base tables. Extended Tables (C) are tables that extend others. Custom Tables (D) can extend base or core tables.

questions.stem: Which of the following statement describes the purpose of an Order Guide?

options.text: Order Guides restrict the number of items in an order to only one item per request
Order Guide provide a list of guidelines for Administrators on how to set up item variables
Order Guide provide the ability to order multiple, related items as one request
Order Guides take the user directly to the checkout without prompting for information

questions.explanation: An Order Guide provides the ability to order multiple, related catalog items as a single request (C). It does not restrict to one item (A) or provide admin setup guidelines (B). Order Guides do prompt users for item-specific information (D is wrong).

questions.stem: Which tool is used to have conversations with logged-in users in real-time?
questions.explanation: Connect Chat is the real-time messaging tool for conversations with logged-in users (A). Now Messenger (B) is not a ServiceNow product. User Presence (C) shows online status indicators. Comments (D) are asynchronous form notes, not real-time conversations.

questions.stem: Which of the following concepts are associated with the ServiceNow CMDB? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: The CMDB is associated with: Service Processes (A), Tables and Fields (C — CIs stored in tables), A Database (D — CMDB is a database), and Dependency View (E — graphical CI relationship visualization). User Permissions (B) are managed by ACLs/roles, not a CMDB concept.

questions.stem: What is a formatter? Select one of the following.

options.text: A formatter allows you to configure applications on your instance
A formatter is a form element used to display information that is not a field in the record
A formatter allows you to populate fields automatically
A formatter is a set of conditions applied to a table to help find and work with data

questions.explanation: A formatter is a form element that displays information that is not a field in the record (B) — for example CI relationships or activity streams. It does not configure applications (A), auto-populate fields (C), or filter data (D — that describes condition builders).

questions.stem: When searching using the App Navigator search field, what can be returned? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: Searching returns: Names of Applications and Modules combined (A), Names of Modules alone (B), Names of Applications alone (C), and Favorites (D). History Records (E) appear in the History section, not filter results. Dashboard Gauge Titles (F) are not returned.

questions.stem: Which technique is used to get information from a series of referenced fields from different tables?
questions.explanation: Dot-walking accesses data from referenced fields across related tables (C) — e.g., incident.caller_id.department traverses the reference to get the caller's department. Table-Walking (A), Sys_ID Pulling (B), and Record-Hopping (D) are not valid ServiceNow terms.

questions.stem: What is a schema map?

options.text: A schema map enables administrators to define records from specific tables as trouble sources for Configuration Items
A schema map graphically organizes the visual task boards for the CMDB
A schema map graphically displays the Configuration Items that support a business service
A schema map displays the details of tables and their relationships in a visual manner, allowing administrators to view and easily access different parts of the database schema

questions.explanation: A schema map visually displays tables and their relationships, allowing admins to view and navigate the database schema (D). It is not for identifying trouble sources for CIs (A), organizing visual task boards (B), or showing CI dependency views (C).

questions.stem: Which one of the following statements best describes the purpose of an Update Set?

options.text: An Update Set allows administrators to group a series of changes into a named set and then move this set as a unit to other systems
By default, an Update Set includes customizations, Business Rules, and homepages
An Update Set is a group of customizations that is moved from Production to Development
By default, the changes included in an Update Set are visible only in the instance to which they are applied

questions.explanation: An Update Set groups a series of changes into a named set and moves them as a unit to other systems (A). Homepages are not included by default (B is wrong). Update Sets move from Dev to Production, not the reverse (C is wrong). Complete sets should stay Complete (D is wrong).

questions.stem: Which of the following can be customized through the Basic Configuration UI 16 module? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: This module allows customizing Banner Image (A), Browser Tab Title (C), and System Date Format (D). Record Number Format (B) is configured separately. Form Header Size (E) is not a Basic Configuration UI 16 option.

questions.stem: What is the function of user impersonation?
questions.explanation: User impersonation is used for testing and visibility (A) — admins impersonate another user to see exactly what that user sees and test access controls. It is not for verbose logging (B), custom perspectives (C), or unlocking application lists (D).

questions.stem: What information does the System Dictionary contain?

options.text: The human-readable labels and language settings
The definition for each table and column
The information on how tables relate to each other
The language dictionary used for spell checking

questions.explanation: The System Dictionary contains the definition for each table and column (data types, default values, labels, attributes) (B). Human-readable labels are in language files (A). Table relationships are in the Schema Map (C). Language spell-check dictionary (D) is not a ServiceNow concept.

questions.stem: When working on a form, what is the difference between Insert and Update operations?

options.text: Insert creates a new record and Update saves changes, both remain on the form
Insert creates a new record and Update saves changes, both exit the form
Insert saves changes and exits the form, Update saves changes and remains on the form
Insert saves changes and remains on the form, Update saves changes and exits the form

questions.explanation: Insert creates a new record and exits the form; Update saves changes to the existing record and also exits the form (B). Both operations exit the form. Insert does not remain on the form (A). Descriptions in C and D swap or misstate the behaviors.

questions.stem: How is the Event Log different from the Event Registry?

options.text: Event Log contains generated Events, the Event Registry is a table of Event definitions
Event Log is formatted in the Log style, the Event Registry displays different fields
Event Log lists Events that were triggered by integrations, the Event Registry lists the Events that were triggered during the day (24-hour period)
Event Log is the same as the Event Registry

questions.explanation: The Event Log contains generated/fired event instances (A). The Event Registry is a table of event definitions/templates. They are not just format differences (B). Triggered-by-integrations vs triggered-during-the-day (C) is incorrect. They are different tables, not the same (D).

questions.stem: What is a Dictionary Override?

options.text: A Dictionary Override is an incoming customer update in an Update Set which applies to the same objects as a newer local customer update
A Dictionary Override is the addition, modification, or removal of anything that could have an effect on IT services
A Dictionary Override is a task within a flow that requests an action before the flow can continue
A Dictionary Override sets field properties in extended tables

questions.explanation: A Dictionary Override sets field properties in extended tables (D), allowing customization of inherited fields for a specific child table. It is not an incoming Update Set conflict (A), a change record (B), or an approval task in a flow (C).

questions.stem: Which group of permissions is used to control Application and Module access?
questions.explanation: Roles control which Applications and Modules a user can access in the App Navigator (C). Access Control Rules (A) protect row/column/table data access. UI Policies (B) control field behavior on forms. Assignment Rules (D) auto-assign records to users or groups.

questions.stem: What is a Record Producer?

options.text: A Record Producer is a type of Catalog Item that is used for Requests, not Services
A Record Producer creates user records
A Record Producer is a type of Catalog Item that provides easy ordering by bundling requests
A Record Producer is a type of a Catalog Item that allows users to create task-based records from the Service Catalog

questions.explanation: A Record Producer is a type of Catalog Item that allows end users to create task-based records (e.g., incidents) from the Service Catalog (D). It is not for creating user records (B) or bundling requests like Order Guides (C). It is not limited to Requests only (A).

questions.stem: Create Incident, Password Reset, and Report outage: what do these services in the Service Catalog have in common?

options.text: They direct the user to a record producer
They direct the user to a catalog property
They direct the user to a catalog UI policy
They direct the user to a catalog client script

questions.explanation: Create Incident, Password Reset, and Report Outage all direct users to Record Producers (A) — catalog items that create task-based records. They do not lead to catalog properties (B), UI policies (C), or client scripts (D).

questions.stem: What is the Import Set Table?

options.text: A table where data will be placed, post-transformation
A staging area for imported records
A repository for Update Set information

questions.explanation: The Import Set Table is the staging area where imported records are held before transformation (C). Data is placed into target tables after transformation (A). Transform Maps determine relationships (B) but are not the table itself. Update Set information (D) is in a different area.

questions.stem: What is a characteristic of importing data into ServiceNow?

options.text: An existing Transform Map can be used one time on the same import set
Coalesce fields are used only after running Transform
Any user can manage and set up import sets
An existing Transform Map can be used multiple times on the same import set

questions.explanation: A Transform Map can be used multiple times on the same import set (D) — you can re-run transforms to update or correct data. It is not one-time use only (A). Coalesce is checked during transform execution (B). Admin role is required, not any user (C).

questions.stem: What module in the Service Catalog application does an Administrator access to begin creating a new item?
questions.explanation: An Administrator accesses the Maintain Items module (B) to create new catalog items. Path: Service Catalog > Catalog Definitions > Maintain Items. Maintain Categories (A) is for category management. Content Items (C) and Items (D) are not the correct module names.

questions.stem: Which of the following allows a user to edit field values in a list without opening the form?
questions.explanation: The List Editor allows users to edit field values directly in a list view without opening the form (C). Data Editor (A) is not a standard ServiceNow feature. Edit Menu (B) refers to form actions. Form Designer (D) is for designing form layouts, not editing list records.

questions.stem: Which three Variable Types can be added to a Service Catalog Item?

options.text: Number List, Single Line Text, and Reference
Multiple Choice, Select Box, and Checkbox

questions.explanation: Multiple Choice, Select Box, and Checkbox (D) are valid variable types. True/False with Ordered (A) and Number List combinations (B, C) are not standard. The catalog variable type list includes Select Box, Multiple Choice, Checkbox, Single Line Text, Reference, etc.

questions.stem: How are Workflows moved between instances?

options.text: Workflows are moved using Update Sets
Workflows are moved using Transform Maps
Workflows are moved using Application Sets
Workflows cannot be moved between instances

questions.explanation: Workflows are moved between instances using Update Sets (A) — by checking out and republishing workflows to include them in an update set. Transform Maps (B) are for data import. Application Sets (C) are not a ServiceNow concept. Workflows can be moved (D is wrong).

questions.stem: The baseline Service Catalog homepage contains links to which of the following components?

options.text: Record Producers, Order Guides, and Catalog Items
Order Guides, Item Variables, and flows
Order Guides, Catalog Items, and flows
Record Producers, Order Guides, and Item Variables

questions.explanation: The baseline Service Catalog homepage contains links to Record Producers, Order Guides, and Catalog Items (A). Item Variables (B, D) are configuration elements within items, not homepage links. Flows (B, C) are fulfillment processes, not homepage components.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true when a new table is created by extending another table?

options.text: The new table archives the parent table and assumed its roles in the database
The new table inherits all of the Business Rules, Client Scripts, and UI Policies of the parent table, but none of the existing fields
The new table inherits all of the fields of the parent table and can also contain new fields unique to itself
The new table inherits all of the fields, but does not inherit Access Control rules, Client Scripts, and UI Policies of the parent table

questions.explanation: When a table extends another, it inherits all fields from the parent AND can have new fields unique to itself (C). It does not archive the parent (A). It also inherits Business Rules/Client Scripts/UI Policies (B is wrong about no fields). ACLs are also inherited (D is wrong).

questions.stem: Where can Admins check which release is running on an ServiceNow instance?
questions.explanation: Admins can check which ServiceNow release is running by navigating to the Stats module (B) — via stats.do. Memory Stats (A) shows server memory. System.upgraded (C) is not a standard navigable table view. Transactions log (D) shows transaction history, not release info.

questions.stem: A knowledge article must be which of the following states to display to a user?
questions.explanation: A knowledge article must be in the Published state (A) to be visible to end users. Draft (B) articles are only visible to contributors. Retired (C) articles are removed from public view. Reviewed (D) is not a standard ServiceNow knowledge article state.

questions.stem: What is the name of the conversational bot platform that provides assistance to help users obtain information, make decisions, and perform common tasks?
questions.explanation: Virtual Agent is the conversational bot platform that helps users obtain information, make decisions, and perform common tasks (C). Answer Agent (A) is not a ServiceNow product. Live Feed (B) is a social collaboration tool. Connect Chat (D) is real-time user-to-user messaging.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of a Related List?

options.text: To dot-walk to a core table

questions.explanation: A Related List presents related records from another table that have a relationship to the current record (D). It displays a one-to-many relationship (A describes the relationship type, not purpose). It does not enable dot-walking (B) or present related fields within the record (C).

questions.stem: Which one of the following statements describes the purpose of a Service Catalog flow?

options.text: A Service Catalog flow generates three basic components: item variable types, tasks, and approvals
Although a Service Catalog flow cannot send notifications, the flow drives complex fulfillment processes
A Service Catalog flow is used to drive complex fulfillment processes and sends notifications to defined users or groups
A Service Catalog flow generates three basic components: item variable types, tasks, and notifications

questions.explanation: A Service Catalog flow drives complex fulfillment processes and sends notifications to defined users or groups (C). It does not only generate variable types, tasks, and approvals (A). It does send notifications (B is incorrect). D mislabels what it generates.

questions.stem: Which term best describes something that is created, has worked performed upon it, and is eventually moved to a state of closed?
questions.explanation: A Task is created, has work performed upon it, and is eventually moved to a closed state (D). The Task [task] table is the core base for Incidents, Problems, Changes, etc. Reports (A) are output documents. Flows (B) are automation processes. Events (C) are system notifications/triggers.

questions.stem: Which are valid Service Now User Authentication Methods? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Valid ServiceNow user authentication methods: Local database (B), LDAP (C) for directory integration, and SSO (D) using SAML. XML feed (A) is a data format, not an auth method. FTP authentication (E) is not a ServiceNow authentication option.

questions.stem: Access Control rules may be defined with which of the following permission requirements? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Access Control rules use three types of permission requirements on the ACL form: Roles (A), Conditional Expressions (B), and Scripts (D). Assignment Rules (C) auto-assign work. User Criteria (E) is for Service Catalog access. Groups (F) are not a separate ACL permission type.

questions.stem: Which section of the ServiceNow UI allows you to perform a global search?
questions.explanation: The Banner Frame at the top of the ServiceNow UI contains the global search field (B). The Application Navigator (A) is the left panel for app/module navigation. The List pane (C) displays record lists. The Content frame (D) is the main area showing forms and lists.

questions.stem: How do you make a list filter available to everyone?

options.text: Make active, assign a name, and save
Assign a group, set visibility, and save
Assign a name, set visibility, and save
Make active, set visibility, and save

questions.explanation: To make a list filter available to everyone, assign a name (so it can be referenced), set visibility to global/Everyone, and save (C). Making it active only (A) does not share it. Assigning a group (B) limits it to that group. Active + visibility (D) omits the required name.

questions.stem: What would NOT appear in the Application Navigator if `service` is typed into the filter field?
questions.explanation: When "service" is typed in the filter, modules/apps containing that word are returned. Business Services (A), Self-Service (B), and Service Portal (C) all contain "service". "Incident > Assigned to me" (D) contains neither "service" — it would NOT appear.

questions.stem: Which of the following is used to categorize, flag, and locate records?
questions.explanation: Tags are used to categorize, flag, and locate records in ServiceNow (C). You can tag any record and search/filter by tags. Search (A) retrieves records but does not tag them. Favorites (B) bookmark navigation items. Bookmarks (D) are not a standard record-management feature.

questions.stem: Which tool should be used to populate commonly used fields in a form?
questions.explanation: A Template is used to pre-populate commonly used field values in a form (A). It allows predefined sets of field values. Reference Qualifier (B) filters reference field lookups. Formatter (C) displays non-field info on a form. Assignment Rule (D) auto-assigns records.

questions.stem: How is a group defined in ServiceNow?

options.text: A group is one record stored in the Group Type [sys_user_group_type] table
A group is one record stored in the Group [sys_user_group] table
A group defines a set of users that share the same location
A group defines a set of users that share the same job title

questions.explanation: A group in ServiceNow is one record stored in the Group [sys_user_group] table (B). The Group Type [sys_user_group_type] table (A) stores types of groups, not the groups themselves. Groups are not defined by shared location (C) or shared job title (D).

questions.stem: What is a role in ServiceNow?

options.text: A role is one record in the Role [user_sys_role] table
A role is a set of modules for a particular application
A role is one record in the Role [sys_user_role] table
A role is a persona used in Live Feed Chat

questions.explanation: A role is one record stored in the Role [sys_user_role] table (C). Option A has the wrong table name (user_sys_role — reversed). Roles are not sets of modules for an application (B — that describes applications). Roles are not Live Feed personas (D).

questions.stem: What is a Notification?

options.text: A new Knowledge article created by a Business Rule
A tool for alerting users that events that concern them have occurred
A message through Connect related to a Change Request

questions.explanation: A Notification is a tool for alerting users that events concerning them have occurred (B) — typically via email, SMS, or push. It is not a Knowledge article created by a Business Rule (A). A Connect message about a change (C) describes a chat message. An email attachment (D) is not a notification.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is NOT a type of Visual Task Board?
questions.explanation: The three VTB types are Flexible (A) — user-configurable columns, Freeform (B) — cards placed anywhere freely, and Guided (D) — pre-defined by admin. Feature (C) is not a valid Visual Task Board type and would NOT appear as an option.

questions.stem: What is (are) best practice(s) regarding users/groups/roles? (Choose two.)

options.text: You should never assign roles to groups.
You should assign roles to users.
You should add users to groups.
You should assign roles to groups.

questions.explanation: Best practices are: add users to groups (C) and assign roles to groups (D). This manages permissions efficiently at the group level. You should NOT assign roles directly to individual users (B is a bad practice). Never assign roles to groups (A) is incorrect.

questions.stem: What are two ways to generate an Event? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Events can be generated by Business Rules (A) using gs.eventQueue(), and Workflows (B) via the Create Event activity. Log entries (C) record system activity but do not generate events. Knowledge article publication (D) does not directly generate platform events.

questions.stem:
Which core table in the ServiceNow platform provides a series of standard fields used on each of the tables that extend it, such as the Incident [incident] and
Problem [problem] tables?
questions.explanation: The Task [task] table is the core table providing standard fields (state, assigned_to, short_description, etc.) used by all extending tables including Incident and Problem (A). Assignment (B), Service (C), and Workflow (D) tables do not play this core role.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements describes how data is organized in a table?

options.text: A column is a field in the database and a record is one user
A column is one field and a record is one row
A column is one field and a record is one column
A column contains data from one user and a record is one set of fields

questions.explanation: A column represents one field (data attribute) and a record represents one row (a single entry/instance) in a table (B). A record is not a user (A). A column is not a record (C). Data does not belong to one user per column (D).

questions.stem: What is a sys_id?

options.text: Unique 32-character identifier that is assigned to every record
Unique 64-character identifier that is assigned to every record

questions.explanation: The sys_id is a unique 32-character GUID identifier automatically assigned to every record in ServiceNow (A). It is not a Business Rule type (B or C). It is not 64 characters — the standard GUID is 32 hexadecimal characters (D is wrong).

questions.stem: When creating a global custom table named `abc`, what is the table name that is automatically assigned by the platform?
questions.explanation: When a global custom table named "abc" is created, the platform automatically assigns it "u_abc" (C) — the "u_" prefix denotes user-created/custom tables. snc_abc (A) is used for some ServiceNow-internal tables. sys_abc (D) is for system tables. "abc" (B) is not used for custom tables.

questions.stem: Access Control rules may provide access security for which of the following database objects?

options.text: For a specific role, group, or user
For a specific row, column, or table
For a specific CMDB Configuration item

questions.explanation: Access Control rules provide access security for specific rows (records), columns (fields), and tables (B). Option A describes who the rule applies to (roles/groups/users), not what objects are secured. Options C and D are too narrow in scope.

questions.stem: What is the primary application used to load data into ServiceNow?
questions.explanation: System Import Sets (C) is the primary application for loading data into ServiceNow from external sources. Service Level Management (A) manages SLAs. Configuration (B) is for CMDB administration. System Update Sets (D) move customizations, not data.

questions.stem: Which of the following steps can be used to import new data into ServiceNow from a spreadsheet?

options.text: Load Data, Create Transform Map, Run Transform
Define Data Source, Select Transform Map, Run Transform
Select Import Set, Select Transform Map, Run Transform

questions.explanation: To import data from a spreadsheet: Load Data (upload file to Import Set) → Create Transform Map (map source to target fields) → Run Transform (execute the mapping) (B). Options A, C, and D have incorrect step sequences or names.

questions.stem: Which tool is used for creating dependencies between configuration items in the CMDB?
questions.explanation: The CI Relationship Editor is the tool used to create dependencies (relationships) between configuration items in the CMDB (A). CMDB Builder (B) is not standard. CI Service Manager (C) manages service CIs. CI Class Manager (D) manages CI class definitions.

questions.stem: What is the difference between a UI Policy and Data Policy?

options.text: Data Policies run when data is entered through the form, by an Import Set, or by web services, while UI Policies are set only by web services
Data Policies can be converted into UI Policies, but UI Policies cannot be converted into Data Policies
Data Policies run regardless of how data is entered into ServiceNow, while UI Policies are used for form interactions
Data Policies run only after UI Policies run successfully

questions.explanation: Data Policies run regardless of how data enters ServiceNow (forms, Import Sets, web services, APIs), while UI Policies only apply to form interactions (C). Data Policies are not limited to web services (A). Data Policies can convert to UI Policies (B). Data Policies do not depend on UI Policies running first (D).

questions.stem: Which one of the following is an accurate list of changes that are captured in an Update Set?

options.text: Changes made to: tables, forms, schedules, and client scripts
Changes made to: tables, forms, Business Rules, and data records
Changes made to: tables, forms, groups, and configuration items (CIs)
Changes made to: table, forms, views, and fields

questions.explanation: Update Sets capture changes to tables, forms, views, and fields (D). They do NOT capture data records (B includes data — wrong). They do NOT capture CI data or groups (C). While client scripts (A) can be captured, D is the most accurate standard answer.

questions.stem: What are the steps to retrieve an Update Set?

options.text: Verify Update Set is Complete, Retrieve, Preview, Apply
Verify Update Set is Complete, Test Connection, Apply
Verify Update Set is Complete, Test Connection, Commit
Verify Update Set is Complete, Retrieve, Preview, Commit

questions.explanation: Steps to retrieve an Update Set: Verify Complete → Retrieve from remote instance → Preview (check conflicts) → Commit (apply) (D). "Apply" is not the correct term (A). "Test Connection" is not a retrieval step (B, C). The final step is Commit, not Apply.

questions.stem: IntegrationHub enables execution of third-party APIs as a part of a flow. These integrations are referred to as
questions.explanation: Third-party API integrations in IntegrationHub are called Spokes (B) — scoped applications containing actions for a specific system. An action (A) is a single step within a spoke. A connection (C) is the credential/endpoint config. Integration step (D) is a generic term.

questions.stem: Which of the following protects applications by identifying and restricting access to available files and data?
questions.explanation: Application Scope protects applications by identifying and restricting access to available application files and data (D). This is the exact definition from platform documentation. Application Configuration (A) is too generic. Verbose Log (B) is for debugging. Access Control Rules (C) protect data records, not application files.

questions.stem: Which one statement correctly describes Access Control rule evaluation?

options.text: Table access rules are evaluated from the general to the specific
If more than one rule applies to a record, the older rule is evaluated first
If a row level rule and a field level rule exist, both rules must be true before an operation is allowed
The role with the most permissions evaluates the rules first.

questions.explanation: If both a row-level ACL and field-level ACL exist, both must evaluate to true before the operation is allowed (C). ACLs are evaluated from specific to general, not general to specific (A is wrong). The more specific rule applies — not the older rule (B). Role permissions do not determine evaluation order (D).

questions.stem:
ServiceNow contains a resource which provides the following:
✑ A standard and shared set of service related definitions across ServiceNow products and platform that will enable and support true service level reporting.
✑ A CMDB framework across our products and platform that will enable and support multiple configuration strategies.
What resource do these statements describe?
questions.explanation: The Common Services Data Model (CSDM) provides a standard, shared set of service definitions and a CMDB framework supporting multiple configuration strategies (A). ITSM (B) is a set of IT service processes. CMDB (C) is the database itself. ITIL (D) is an industry framework.

questions.stem: An IT manager is responsible for the Network and Hardware assignment groups, each group contains 5 team members. These team members are working on many tasks, but the manager cannot see any tasks on the Service Desk > My Groups Work list. What could explain this?

options.text: The Service Desk > My Groups Work list shows active work tasks that are not yet assigned.
The manager does not have the itil role.
The manager is not a member of the Service Desk group.
The manager is not a member of the Network and Hardware groups.
The Assignment Group manager field is empty.

questions.explanation: This list shows tasks assigned to groups the current user is a MEMBER of. The manager is responsible for the Network and Hardware groups but is not listed as a member (D) — so those group tasks don't appear. Being a group manager is different from being a group member.

questions.stem: What do you need to do before you can use an Application-based trigger in your flow?

options.text: Activate application spoke, and plug-ins as needed
Assign Application trigger role [sn_app_trigger_write] to SME

questions.explanation: Before using an Application-based trigger, activate the application spoke and any required plugins (C). The spoke provides the trigger capability. Activating the spoke alone (A) may be insufficient without plugins. Trigger security rules (B) and assigning a trigger role (D) are not prerequisites.

questions.stem: The ServiceNow platform includes which types of interfaces? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The platform includes three main interface types: Now Mobile Apps (A), Service Portals (D), and Now Platform User Interfaces (E). Agent Control Center (B), Back Office Dashboard (C), and Field Service Taskboard (F) are not standard platform interface categories.

questions.stem: Which of the following are not included in an Update Set, by default? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: NOT included by default: Data/records (B), Schedules (E), Database changes/DDL (F), and Scheduled Jobs (I). Business Rules (D), Client Scripts (J), Views (K), Related Lists (G), Homepages (A), Report Definitions (H), and Published Workflows (C) can be included.

questions.stem:
You are showing your customer a new form that you have created for their new application. They would like to add a field to the form. Where could you do that?
(Choose two.)

options.text: Click on context menu, select Admin view
Right click on form header, select Configure > Form Layout
Click on context menu, select Configure > Form Designer

questions.explanation: Two ways to add a field to a form are: right-click form header > Configure > Form Layout and context menu > Configure > Form Designer. Select Column View, Fields and Columns module, Admin view, and Field Class Manager are not the correct approaches.

questions.stem:
You are showing your customer a new form that you have created for their new application. They would like to add a field to the form. Where could you do that?
(Choose two.)

options.text: Right click on form header, select Configure > Form Layout
Click on context menu, select Configure > Form Designer

questions.explanation: Two ways to add a field to a form are: right-click form header > Configure > Form Layout and context menu > Configure > Form Designer. Select Column View, Fields and Columns module, Admin view, and Field Class Manager are not the correct approaches.

questions.stem: Which ServiceNow resource is a framework that ensures the data your ServiceNow application requires maps correctly to the appropriate CMDB tables?
questions.explanation: The Common Service Data Model (CSDM) is the framework that ensures data maps correctly to the appropriate CMDB tables (A). SMU (B), SSM (C), CMDBCM (D), and CICM (E) are not the resource for this mapping framework. CI Class Manager manages class definitions, not the data mapping framework.

questions.stem: What do you activate when you want to add applications or functionality within your development instance?
questions.explanation: Activate a Plugin to add applications or functionality within a ServiceNow development instance. Plugins are activated via System Definition > Plugins. App Package, Update Pack, Patch, App Key, App Installer, and App Update Set are not valid mechanisms.

questions.stem: What do you activate when you want to add applications or functionality within your development instance?
questions.explanation: Activate a Plugin to add applications or functionality within a ServiceNow development instance. Plugins are activated via System Definition > Plugins. App Package, Update Pack, Patch, App Key, App Installer, and App Update Set are not valid mechanisms.

questions.stem: What field contains a record's 32-character, unique identifier?
questions.explanation: The sys_id field contains the unique 32-character GUID identifier for every record (D). sn_rec_id (A), rec_id (B), u_id (C), sn_gu_id (E), sn_sys_id (F), and id (G) are not the standard ServiceNow field name for the system identifier.

questions.stem: Your company is giving all first line workers a special T-shirt as a recognition for their hard work. Management team wants a way for employees to order the T- shirt, with the ability to specify the preferred size and color. How would you ensure that only first line workers (non-managers) can submit the order?

options.text: Create Record Producer and use the Available For list to specify First Line [sn_first_line] role
Create Catalog Item and use the Not Available list to specify the Manager Group
Create Catalog Item and use the Available For list to specify ITIL [itil] role
Create Order Guide and use the User Criteria list to specify First Line [sn_first_line] role

questions.explanation: Create a Catalog Item with the "Not Available" list specifying the Manager Group (B) — managers cannot see the item, leaving it available only to non-managers. Record Producer (A) creates task records. Available For ITIL role (C) does not exclude managers. Order Guide (D) bundles multiple items.

questions.stem: What is used frequently to move customizations from one instance to another?
questions.explanation: Update Sets are used most frequently to move customizations between instances (A). Code Sets (B), Update Packs (C), Configuration Logs (D), Remote Sets (E), Local Sets (F), and Code Packs (G) are not the standard mechanism for moving customizations.

questions.stem: What icon do you use to change the label on a Favorite?
questions.explanation: The pencil (edit) icon is used to change the label on a Favorite (C). Clock (A) shows history. Hamburger (B) opens a menu. Three dots (D) may show options. Triangle (E) indicates collapsible sections. Star (F) marks/adds favorites but does not rename them.

questions.stem: What needs to be specified, when creating a Business Rule? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: Required fields when creating a Business Rule: Table (B) — which table it applies to, Script to run (E) — JavaScript logic, Timing (H) — before/after/async/display, Condition (I) — when to execute. UI action (A) is for UI Actions. Fields to update (C) are optional. Who can run (D) and Update set (G) are not Business Rule fields.

questions.stem: What feature can track the amount of time that a task has been open, to ensure that tasks are completed within an allotted time?
questions.explanation: Service Level Agreements (B) track the amount of time a task has been open and enforce resolution/response targets. Task Escalation Clock (A) and Response Time Clock (D) are not ServiceNow features. Inactivity Monitor (C) flags inactivity. Business Time Remaining (E) is an SLA field, not the feature itself.

questions.stem: What is a quick way to create a report from a list view?

options.text: Click on filter breadcrumb, drag and drop on the Report > Create New module
Click Funnel, define filter conditions, click Create Report
Click Context Menu, select Create Report
Apply filter, right click on column header, select Bar Chart
Apply filter, right click on column header, select Create Report

questions.explanation: A quick way to create a report from a list view is to apply a filter, then right-click a column header and select Bar Chart (D) to immediately generate a visual report. This is the standard quick-report workflow from a list. Option E incorrectly labels the option as "Create Report" rather than the chart type.

questions.stem: What import utility do you use when the field names on the import set match the name of the fields on the Target table?
questions.explanation: Automatic Mapping matches source to target fields when column names in the import set match field names in the target table exactly.

questions.stem: As an IT employee what interface would you use, if you wanted to browse internal IT documentation, like troubleshooting scripts and FAQs?
questions.explanation: The Knowledge application provides IT documentation and knowledge articles accessible by service desk agents and self-service users.

questions.stem: A new Service Desk employee in Latin America complains that the create dates and times are incorrect on their Incident list. What would you suggest to fix this issue?

options.text: Have them use the gear icon to set the employee's time zone.
Recommend they use Chrome, instead of Explorer.
Use the system properties to correct the instance's time zone.
Have them correct the time zone on their computer.

questions.explanation: Click the Gear icon in the banner to open System Settings, then configure your Time Zone preference under the General tab.

questions.stem: What are three security modules often used by the System Administrator? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: High Security Settings cover System Properties > Security (A), enabling ACLs (E), and activating the High Security Settings module (G).

questions.stem: When testing a catalog item, having a manager approval flows, which of these best practices would you follow? (Choose three.)

options.text: Make sure the latest flows are activated.
Use the instance Incognito setting to quickly toggle between requester and approver.
Impersonate the requester to ensure the form works.
Make sure the requester's user record has a manager specified.
Create and select your Testing Update Set, before starting the test cases.
Use your Admin account, so you can approve the items quickly.

questions.explanation: Best practices for testing a catalog item with manager approval: impersonate the requester (A), activate flows (C), set manager on user record (D).

questions.stem: What is a no-code approach to control the mandatory or read-only state of a form field?
questions.explanation: UI Policy is a no-code tool to make form fields mandatory, read-only, or hidden based on conditions—no scripting required.

questions.stem: When moving multiple update sets at one time, what might you do to facilitate the move?
questions.explanation: To move multiple update sets at once, Merge Update Sets combines them into a single update set before retrieving and committing to the target instance.

questions.stem: When moving multiple update sets at one time, what might you do to facilitate the move?
questions.explanation: Batch Update Sets lets you group multiple related update sets and move them together as a batch to another ServiceNow instance.

questions.stem: What is specified in an Access Control rule?

options.text: Table Schema, CRUD, and User Authentication
Object and Operation being secured; Permissions required to access the object

questions.explanation: Each Access Control specifies the object (table/field), the operation (read/write/create/delete), and the permissions (roles/conditions/scripts) required.

questions.stem: Which icon would you double click, to expand and collapse the list of all Applications and Modules?
questions.explanation: Click the Application icon in the banner to expand or collapse the application navigator panel displayed on the left side of the screen.

questions.stem: What do you call any component that needs to be managed in order to deliver services?
questions.explanation: A Configuration Item (CI) is any component that must be managed in order to deliver an IT service, tracked in the CMDB.

questions.stem: A new service catalog item is being developed, but should only be visible to managers inside the HR Department. What method would you use to fulfill this requirement?

options.text: Specify the Dept_Mgr role on the catalog content block
Add the Department Manager group to the catalog item's user criteria
Add the Department Manager group to the catalog item's ACL
Only publish the item in the HR service catalog
Use a Dept_Mgr ACL on the HR service catalog

questions.explanation: User Criteria on a catalog item controls which users can see and order the item based on attributes such as role, company, group, or location.

questions.stem:
A user wants to create a set of filter conditions, where they want to show records which satisfy two conditions:
✑ Incidents where the state is Closed
✑ Incidents where Assignment Group is Network
After clicking the Funnel icon, what should the user do?

options.text: Define the first condition; click AND button; define second condition; click Run
Define the first condition; click AND button; define second condition; press enter
Define the first condition; click OR button; define second condition; press enter
Define the first condition; click > icon on breadcrumb, define second condition; click Run
Define the first condition; click > icon on breadcrumb, define second condition; press enter

questions.explanation: To filter by multiple conditions, define the first condition, click AND, define the second condition, then click Run to apply the combined filter.

questions.stem:
Access Control rules are applied to a specific table, like the Incident table. What is the object name for a rule that is specific to the Incident table and the Major
Incident field?
questions.explanation: ACL object names for fields use lowercase dot notation: tablename.fieldname. The major_incident field on the Incident table is incident.major_incident.

questions.stem:
Two departments (HR Onboarding and Facilities) have come to you, asking for a way for employees to request event room set up services. The requirements are the same for the form and the task routing to the Facilities' assignment group.
✑ For HR, the item will be used primarily for the Onboarding coordinators, for employee orientation sessions.
✑ For Facilities, the item will be used for anyone in the company who needs room set up services.
However, both departments have their own service catalogs. What do you do, to support these requirements?

options.text: Create one Catalog Item for HR Event Room Set Up and one for Facilities Event Room Set Up; then publish each to the appropriate Catalog.
Create one Catalog Item for Event Room Set Up; then publish to both Catalogs.
Create one Catalog Item for Event Room Set Up; then publish to the Parent Catalog, which is accessible to both HR and Facilities.
Create one Catalog Item for Event Room Set Up; then use ACLs to control access.

questions.explanation: A single catalog item can be published to multiple service catalogs by adding entries to the Catalogs related list on the item record.

questions.stem: After finishing your work on High Security Settings, what do you do to return to normal admin security levels?

options.text: Use System Administration > Normal Security module

questions.explanation: After activating High Security Settings, log out and log back in as a normal admin user to restore standard administrative access.

questions.stem: What type of field allows you to look up values from one other table?
questions.explanation: A Reference field stores a link to a record in another table, letting users look up and select values from the referenced table.

questions.stem: Which module would you use to create a new automation of business logic such as approvals, tasks, and notifications?
questions.explanation: Flow Designer is found at All > Process Automation > Flow Designer and is used to build no-code automated business workflows.

questions.stem: A department manager asks an analyst to build some reports. Where do you recommend the analyst start?
questions.explanation: Navigate to All > Reports > Create New to open the Report Designer, where you select report type, data source, and configure layout options.

questions.stem: What are the steps for applying an update set to an instance?
questions.explanation: The three steps to move an update set: Retrieve (import from remote), Preview (check for conflicts), and Commit (apply to target instance).

questions.stem: When importing spreadsheet data into ServiceNow, in which step does the data get written to the receiving table?
questions.explanation: Run Transform is the step that executes the transform map and writes the imported data from the import set table to the receiving target table.

questions.stem: What would you do, on a list, if you wanted to show the records in groups, based on the column category? (Choose two.)

options.text: On list Context Menu, select Group By > Category
On the Filter Menu, select Group By > Category
Click Group On icon, select Category
On Navigator Filter, type tablename.group.category and press enter
On the Category column title, click Context menu > Group By Category

questions.explanation: To group list records by category, use List Context Menu > Group By > Category (A), or right-click the Category column header and select Group By Category (E).

questions.stem: Which collaboration tool is available from the banner, using the bubble icon?
questions.explanation: Connect Chat is accessed via the bubble icon in the banner. It opens the Connect sidebar for real-time messaging and collaboration with other users.

questions.stem: On the knowledge base record, which tab would you use to define which users are not able to write articles to the knowledge base?
questions.explanation: The Cannot Contribute tab on the knowledge base record defines user criteria for users who are NOT allowed to write articles.

questions.stem: Which features allow you to update multiple records at one time? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Use the List Editor (A) to edit individual fields inline, or select records and use Update Selected Action (E) to update multiple records at one time.

questions.stem: Categories in the knowledge base, by default, can be created and edited by which knowledge workers? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: By default, knowledge base categories can be created and edited by Knowledge Contributors (B) and Knowledge Managers (D).

questions.stem: Which collaboration tool opens a sidebar and allows you to create new conversations with other ServiceNow users?
questions.explanation: Agent Chat opens a sidebar interface that allows service desk users to create new conversations with other ServiceNow users for real-time collaboration.

questions.stem: What module would you use if you wanted to view a list of all of the fields on the Incident table? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Tables & Columns (A) and Dictionary (B) both allow you to view all fields defined for a table, including their types and attributes.

questions.stem: What component causes a flow to run after a record has been created or updated?
questions.explanation: A Record-based trigger causes a flow to run after a record has been created or updated in the specified table.

questions.stem: What type of field is Boolean and appears as a check box?
questions.explanation: The True/False field type is a Boolean that appears as a check box on forms—checked means true, unchecked means false.

questions.stem: Which module is used to access the knowledge bases which are available to you?
questions.explanation: Navigate to All > Self-Service > Knowledge to access the knowledge bases available to the current user.

questions.stem:
A customer requests the following data quality measures be added:
✑ Incident numbers should be read only, on all lists and forms, for all users.
✑ Short Description field should be mandatory, on all records, across all applications, on Insert.
Which type of policy would you use to meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: Data Policy enforces read-only and mandatory rules on all lists and forms for all users, applying across the entire platform regardless of UI.

questions.stem: What type of user (persona) has clearly defined paths and workflows in the platform and have one or more roles (ie itil and approver_user)?
questions.explanation: A Process User has clearly defined paths and workflows in the platform and is assigned one or more functional roles such as itil and approver_user.

questions.stem: Which module would you use to customize your instances banner image, text and colors?
questions.explanation: This module allows administrators to customize the instance banner image, banner text, and interface colors for UI16.

questions.stem: Which database provides a logical model of your company infrastructure by identifying, controlling, maintaining and verifying CIs that exist?
questions.explanation: The Configuration Management Database (CMDB) provides a logical model of company infrastructure by identifying, controlling, maintaining, and verifying CIs.

questions.stem: Which module is used as the first step for importing data?
questions.explanation: Load Data is the first step in the import process. It creates an import set table and populates it with records from the data source file.

questions.stem: When you need to orchestrate business processes across services with little technical user knowledge, which utility would you use?
questions.explanation: Flow Designer enables business process owners to orchestrate business processes across services with a no-code/low-code graphical interface.

questions.stem: When a user reports that they are not able to see modules on the application navigator, what can you do, to see what modules are visible to them?

options.text: Look up their password, so you can login with their account

questions.explanation: Use the Impersonate User feature to log in as another user temporarily, which lets you see exactly what modules and data they can access.

questions.stem: What is a key difference between Reporting and Performance Analytics?

options.text: Performance Analytics contains snapshots of data taken over time; Reporting shows only the data as it is, at the moment the report is run.
Performance Analytics can show trends; Reports cannot.
Reports can be run on a scheduled basis; Performance Analytics cannot.
Performance Analytics data can be published to Dashboards; Reports cannot.
Performance Analytics shows KPIs; Reporting does not.

questions.explanation: Performance Analytics stores snapshots of data over time for trend analysis; Reports show only a current point-in-time view of the data.

questions.stem:
While showing a customer their incident form, they ask to change the Priority values to display their internal terminology P1, P2, P3, P4. They want it to be consistent across all Tasks. How would you do that?
Right click on Priority and select what?
questions.explanation: Right-click the Priority field and select Show Choice List to open the choice list editor and modify the display values like P1, P2, P3, P4.

questions.stem: Your customer would like to create a new template to notify users who are affected by network outages at their site. Which module would you use to create a new notification?
questions.explanation: Navigate to All > System Notification > Email > Notifications to create a new email notification template for any event.

questions.stem: When designing a flow, how do you reference data from a record, in that flow?

options.text: Drag the table icon onto the flow definition
Use the condition builder to specify the desired values
Specify the source table on the data pill related list
Drag the data pill onto the flow definition
Add the table reference using the slush bucket

questions.explanation: To reference record data inside a flow, drag a data pill from the Data pill picker onto the flow definition where the value is needed.

questions.stem: On the Reports page, what sections allow you to see which reports are visible to different audiences? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: The Reports page organizes reports by audience sections: Group (A), My reports (C), Global (F), and All (I) to show which reports are visible to whom.

questions.stem: Which tool is used to define relationships between fields in an import set table and a target table?
questions.explanation: A Transform Map defines the relationships between fields in an import set (staging) table and the target ServiceNow table for data migration.

questions.stem: Which ServiceNow capability provides assistance to help users obtain information, make decisions, and perform common work tasks via a messaging interface?
questions.explanation: Virtual Agent provides AI-powered assistance to help users obtain information, make decisions, and perform common tasks via a messaging interface.

questions.stem: Which feature allows you to automate business logic for a particular application or process such as approvals, tasks notifications, and record operations?
questions.explanation: Flows automate business logic for applications and processes, including approvals, tasks, notifications, and record operations without manual scripting.

questions.stem: From a form, what would you click to add additional fields to the form? (Choose two.)

options.text: Right click on header > Add > Field
Right click on header > Configure > UX Dashboard

questions.explanation: To add fields to a form, right-click the form header and select Configure > Form Layout (B) or Configure > Form Design (C) from the context menu.

questions.stem: What is the name of the table relationship, where two or more tables are related in a bi-directional relationship, so that the related records are visible from both tables in a related list?
questions.explanation: A Many-to-Many relationship links two or more tables bi-directionally so related records are visible from both tables in a related list.

questions.stem: On a Form header, what is the three bar icon called?
questions.explanation: The three-bar icon (hamburger icon) on a form header is called the Additional Actions menu or Context Menu—it provides form-level configuration options.

questions.stem: Group records are stored in which table?
questions.explanation: Group records are stored in the Group [sys_user_group] table. This is the standard table name for ServiceNow user groups.

questions.stem: What function do you use to add buttons, links, and context menu items on forms and lists?
questions.explanation: UI Actions are used to add buttons, links, and context menu items to forms and lists, enabling custom actions when clicked.

questions.stem: On a Business Rule, the When setting determines at what point the rule executes. What are the options for specifying that timing?
questions.explanation: The When field on a Business Rule determines execution timing. Options are: Before, After, Async (asynchronous), and Display.

questions.stem: What are different types of Data Sources, which may be imported into ServiceNow? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: ServiceNow supports multiple data source types: Local files such as XML/CSV/Excel (A), JDBC connections (D), Network Servers (E), and LDAP (F).

questions.stem: What are the components that make up a filter condition? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: A filter condition has three components: Field (E, what to filter on), Operator (A, the comparison type), and Value (C, the comparison value).

questions.stem: When impersonating a user for testing purposes, what is the best way to return the instance, logged in with your user account?

options.text: Turn your computer off and on again

questions.explanation: When testing as another user, click End Impersonation in the banner to return to your original admin account without logging out.

questions.stem: What controls the publishing and retiring process for knowledge articles?
questions.explanation: The publishing and retiring process for knowledge articles is controlled by Workflows, which define the approval and state transition steps.

questions.stem: What type of query allows you to filter list data using normal words, instead of the condition builder?
questions.explanation: Natural Language Query allows users to filter list data using plain English words instead of the condition builder for faster searching.

questions.stem: Tables may have a One to Many relationships. From the Service Catalog, what are examples of tables having a one to many relationships? (Choose three.)

options.text: One Approval can have many Requests
One Request can have many Requested Items
One Requested Item can have many Approvals
One Requested Item can have many Catalog Tasks
One Cart can have many Requests

questions.explanation: One-to-many examples: one Request has many RITMs (B), one RITM has many Approvals (C), one RITM has many Catalog Tasks (D).

questions.stem: On a filter condition, which component is always a choice list?
questions.explanation: The Operator component of a filter condition is always a choice list—it presents pre-defined comparison options like is, contains, starts with, etc.

questions.stem: A Role is defined as what?

options.text: A set of user access policies
A set of access control rules

questions.explanation: A Role is defined as a collection of permissions. Roles are assigned to users or groups to grant access to applications, modules, and records.

questions.stem: A user is complaining that they are seeing a blank page, when they click Create New, from your custom Inventory application. You have confirmed that they can see the Inventory application, and the Create New module on the application navigator. What could be the cause of this issue?

options.text: Create New module has a broken link
User should be using Chrome instead of Explorer for their browser
User has read role, but not the write role on the Inventory table

questions.explanation: A blank page on Create New typically means the user has the read role to see the module but lacks the write role needed to create records on the table.

questions.stem: What resource can you use to view details of the tables and configuration items (CIs) associated with a particular use case?

options.text: Common Service Data Model (CSDM) product view

questions.explanation: The Common Service Data Model (CSDM) product view provides a resource showing tables and CIs associated with a particular use case or product.

questions.stem: A manager wants to view a snapshot of month-end Sales performance data, as compared to Sales targets. In addition, the manager wants to be able to see those monthly numbers trended over time, and forecasted into the future. What capability do you suggest for this manager?

options.text: Scheduled Reports, a custom snapshot table, and a Trend report
Scheduled Reports, a custom snapshot table, and a Projection report

questions.explanation: Performance Analytics supports month-end snapshots, trend analysis over time, and forecasting—ideal for monitoring sales vs. targets.

questions.stem: What are advantages of using Flow Designer? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Key advantages of Flow Designer include reducing technical debt (C), less manual scripting (D), and smooth integration with 3rd party systems (E).

questions.stem: Your customer requires that they be able to monitor which users are performing impersonations in their instance. What would you do to meet that requirement?

options.text: Add the role Log Write [sn_log_write] to the Impersonator Group
Create user update set for impersonation tracking
From User icon, select Elevate Roles
On the Impersonator role record, right click and select Create Log

questions.explanation: To monitor impersonations, activate the glide.sys.log_impersonation system property, which logs all impersonation activity in the system log.

questions.stem: When a flow runs an action, it generates a runtime value, which stays the same for the duration of the flow. What is the name of this runtime value?
questions.explanation: When a flow runs an action, it generates a data pill runtime value. This value is produced at runtime and remains constant for the life of that flow.

questions.stem: The wait time for end users is based on the round-trip between the client and the server. What activities are included in the round-trips?
questions.explanation: End-user wait time is measured as the round-trip between client and server, which consists of the Request (client to server) and Response (server to client).

questions.stem: When importing data, what happens to imported rows, if no coalesce field is specified?

options.text: All rows are rejected from the import, as coalesce field is required.
All rows are treated as new records. No existing records are updated.
Duplicate rows are rejected from the import.
All rows are treated as new records, but errors will be flagged in the import log.

questions.explanation: When no coalesce field is specified in a transform map, all imported rows are treated as new records—no existing records are matched or updated.

questions.stem: What is the most common role that has access to almost all platform features, functions, and data?
questions.explanation: The System Administrator [admin] role is the most common role providing access to almost all platform features, functions, and data.

questions.stem: What feature do you use to specify which users are able to access a Service Catalog Item?
questions.explanation: User Criteria is the feature used to specify which users are able to access and order a Service Catalog item based on their attributes.

questions.stem: Which component of a table contains a piece of data for one record?
questions.explanation: A Field is a component of a table that contains a single piece of data for one record, corresponding to a column in the database table.

questions.stem: What type of field has a drop down list, from which you can pick from pre-defined options?
questions.explanation: A Choice field presents a drop-down list of pre-defined options for the user to select from, stored as a value in the database.

questions.stem: User records are stored in which table?
questions.explanation: User records are stored in the User [sys_user] table. This is the standard platform table for all ServiceNow user records.

questions.stem: What ServiceNow feature can be triggered by events, and is used to inform users about activities or updates in ServiceNow?
questions.explanation: Notifications are triggered by platform events and inform users about activities or updates in ServiceNow via email, push, or SMS.

questions.stem: Which ServiceNow capability allows you to provide knowledge articles, via a conversational messaging interface?
questions.explanation: Virtual Agent provides knowledge articles via a conversational messaging interface, enabling self-service through natural language interactions.

questions.stem: Which role can manage multiple knowledge bases?
questions.explanation: The knowledge_admin role can manage multiple knowledge bases, approve articles, and configure knowledge base settings across the platform.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly describes the differences between a Client Script and a Business Rule?

options.text: A Client Script executes before a record is loaded and a Business Rule executes after a record is loaded
A Client Script executes on the server and a Business Rule executes on the client
A Client Script executes on the client and a Business Rule executes on the server
